transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I… I guess I came because I can’t stop noticing this sagging, uneven area around my jaw and neck. People say it looks normal, but I don’t really believe them. It feels like it’s the first thing people see—families, nurses, people at church… anyone looking at me.
How much time would you say you spend thinking about this sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck each day?

A lot, I guess. It’s… on and off through the day, but it feels like I’m always noticing it—my jaw and neck, that sagging uneven part. Even when people say it looks normal, I keep thinking they’re seeing it first.
Is thinking about the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck causing you a lot of distress?

Yes… it does. I mean, I came in because I can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. Even when people tell me it looks normal, I still feel like it’s what families, nurses, or people at church notice first when they look at me.
Is your concern only about how the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck looks, or does it also involve other aspects like its function or health?
It’s really about how it looks. I just… I can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. Even if people say it’s normal, I feel like it’s what they notice first.
Does your perception of the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck ever change, or does it always look the same to you?

It kind of changes depending on the moment, I guess, but… mostly I just can’t stop seeing it. That sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. Even when people tell me it looks normal, I still feel like it’s the first thing they notice.
Do you ever have days where you don't notice the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck at all?

Not really… I mean, maybe I’m distracted sometimes, but mostly I still notice it. That sagging, uneven part around my jaw and neck just kind of catches my eye, and I worry other people see it first too.
Has your concern about the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck affected your ability to work or interact with others?

Yeah… it has, a bit. At work I’ve avoided leading meetings or taking on more supervisory things because I feel like everyone will be looking at my face and neck. And sometimes I get stuck trying to look okay before work, so then I fall behind on paperwork.

I’ve also skipped some book club and walking club things. Getting ready just feels like too much sometimes.
Do you think your sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck has gotten better or worse over time?

I don’t know if it’s actually gotten worse… but I notice it more now. I came in because I just can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. Even when people say it looks normal, I still feel like it’s the first thing people notice.
Have you ever felt completely reassured about the appearance of your jaw and neck after someone told you it looked normal?

No… not completely. Even when someone says it looks normal, it doesn’t really settle it for me. I still feel like that sagging around my jaw and neck is what people notice first… families, nurses, people at church.
Have you ever had a moment where you felt okay about the appearance of your jaw and neck, even if it was just for a brief time?

Maybe for a minute here or there, but… not really. I came in because I just can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. Even if someone says it looks normal, I still feel like families, nurses, or people at church notice it right away.
Have you ever considered seeking a professional opinion, like a dermatologist or plastic surgeon, about the appearance of your jaw and neck?

I… I’ve thought about it, yes. Mostly because I came in not being able to stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. Even when folks tell me it looks normal, I still feel like it’s what families, nurses, or people at church notice first.
Have you avoided any social or occupational activities because of your concerns about the appearance of your jaw and neck?

Yes… some. At work I’ve turned down chances to help lead meetings or do more of the supervisory parts, because I feel like people will be staring at my face and neck. And I’ve gotten behind on paperwork sometimes because I get stuck trying to make myself look… presentable.

I’ve also skipped some book club and walking club things. Getting ready just feels like too much.
Is there anything that you think could be done to fix the appearance of the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck?

I don’t know… I guess if someone could just make that sagging, uneven part not stand out so much. That’s what I can’t stop seeing around my jaw and neck.

Even when people say it looks normal, it doesn’t feel normal to me. It feels like it’s the first thing families, nurses, or people at church notice when they look at me.
Have you stopped doing anything important to you because of your concerns about the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck?

Yes… I guess I have. I’ve passed up leading meetings or doing more supervisory things at work because I worry people will be looking at my face and neck. And sometimes I get behind on paperwork because I’m stuck trying to look presentable.

I’ve also stopped going to some book club and walking club things. Getting ready just feels like too much.
Have you ever felt like your concerns about the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck have significantly impacted your overall quality of life?

Yes… I think it has. I don’t like saying that, but it’s affected work and things I used to do.

I’ve passed up chances to help lead meetings or take on more supervisory parts because I worry people will be looking at my face and neck. And sometimes I fall behind on paperwork because I get stuck trying to make myself look presentable.

I’ve also stopped going to some book club and walking club things. Getting ready just feels like too much sometimes.
Do you think there's anything that could change your perception of the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck?

I don’t know. Maybe if I could really believe people when they say it looks normal… but I just can’t seem to.

I came in because I can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. It feels like it’s the first thing people notice, even at church or around families and nurses.
Is your concern about your appearance limited to the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck, or do you feel unattractive in general?

It’s mostly that area… my jaw and neck. I mean, I don’t feel great about how I look overall sometimes, but what I can’t stop seeing is that sagging, uneven spot.

Even when people say it looks normal, I feel like it’s the first thing families, nurses, or people at church notice when they look at me.
Do you think you would feel attractive if the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck were to completely disappear?

Maybe… I don’t know. I think I’d feel better, at least.

It’s just that I can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven part around my jaw and neck. Even when people tell me it looks normal, I still feel like it’s the first thing families, nurses, or people at church notice.
Do you think you would still feel unattractive even if the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck were completely fixed?

I’m not sure. I think if that part was fixed, I’d feel better… but right now I just can’t stop seeing that spot around my jaw and neck. Even when people say it looks normal, it feels like it’s what everyone notices first.
